extracted.intended_audience: editors, authors, proofreaders, compositors, and typographers working for academic or professional presses
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for typographical style, composition, and editorial practice as used by the University of Chicago Press (early-20th-century Manual of Style). Covers capitalization, italics, quotations, spelling, punctuation, divisions, footnotes, indexing, tables, technical terms, proofreader practice, and type specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for Composition (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: A codification of typographical rules employed by the University of Chicago Press to govern official printing and publications; rules are meant for the average case and are to be applied with elasticity and discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that regulations are not absolute, exceptions may be made for subject-matter, author preference, or typographical contingency; applicability and common sense emphasized over rigid consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization (general section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules governing which words and classes of words should be capitalized in publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains numbered rules (1–53 and many subrules) with examples and exceptions; includes specialized treatments for foreign titles, institutional names, scientific names, biblical references, and headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Italics (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when to set words, titles, technical terms, and other items in italic type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in contents as a distinct section (page 25). Examples and conventions for typesetting titles, foreign words, technical names, scientific names, and emphasis are provided in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for quoting, punctuation with quotations, capitalization in quotations, and block/inline quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a distinct section (page 33) with specific rules such as capitalization after colons, first word of cited speech, and treatment of quotations closely connected to preceding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for spelling, including lists of words with variant spellings and rules on when to spell out or abbreviate certain terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules and lists (page 37 and 92–120) on spelling of numbers, names, decades, 'United States', 'Saint', possessives, and other special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing punctuation usage throughout printed works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a section (page 50) covering punctuation specifics referenced throughout the manual (e.g., commas, periods, colons, dashes, use with quotations and headings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on subdivisions, enumeration, headings, and the structure of sections, chapters, and lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses numbering, capitalization and punctuation of enumeration items, and indentation/notation schemes (page 81 and various rule references such as 36, 176).

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the composition, placement, and formatting of footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules include numbering, punctuation, capitalization, and typesetting notes (page 88; references elsewhere such as superior figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and conventions for creating indexes and entries, including use of superior figures, treatment of special characters, and indexing names with particles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed guidance appears (page 92 and index sections 232–240 series) including conventions for small caps, cross-references, and special-language treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular Work (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for designing and typesetting tables, including open vs. ruled tables, column headings, use of braces, leaders, footnotes to tables, and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when to use open vs ruled tables, column headline styles, continued tables, and specimen tables (page 95 and rules 241–50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Terms (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typographical treatment of technical terms, special characters, and definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when to use quotation marks for technical terms, how to set special signs and accents, and provides lists of typographical terms (page 103 and 251–94).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to Authors and Editors (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice for authors and editors submitting and preparing manuscripts for the Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a distinct appendix-like section (page 121) giving procedural and stylistic guidance to contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to Proofreaders (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and practical rules targeted at proofreaders about common practices and how to mark corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes proofreading priorities, common errors to watch for, and reference to proofreader's marks (page 125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to Copyholders (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for copyholders (those following proofs) on how to check and hold copy for typesetters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses duties and expectations of copyholders (page 130).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader's Marks (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard marks used by proofreaders to indicate corrections to type and layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full list of marks is provided (page 133) to ensure consistent correction communication between proofreader and compositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens of Types in Use (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimen pages showing available typefaces, sizes, and styles used by the Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete samples (pages 135 onward) to guide selection of type and display of special characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotype Accents and Special Monotype Characters (section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventory and instructions for setting accents and special characters on the monotype machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes lists and specimen pages (pages 275–84) for correct composition of accented and special characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and Index-to-Manual (sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexes covering the manual's content and types used, aiding quick reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes an index to the manual and an index to types, signs, and subjects (pages 283–299 and onward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 1: Proper nouns and adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize proper nouns and adjectives (e.g., George, America, Englishman; Elizabethan, French).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize verbs derived from proper names with specialized meanings (to boycott, to pasteurize) nor certain scientific/trade terms (volt, ampere) when used in their special sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 2: Epithets used as substitutes or affixed
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize epithets used as substitutes for proper names or affixed to a name (e.g., the Pretender, Bloody Mary, Richard the Lion-hearted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided to show usage when epithet functions as part of the name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 3: Particles in French names and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize particles in French names (le, la, de, du) when not preceded by a Christian name or title; do not capitalize them when preceded by such name/title (Le Bossu vs. Rene le Bossu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes personal-preference exceptions for Dutch 'van' and similar particles (e.g., Henry van Dyke).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 4: Generic geographic terms as part of names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize generic terms that form an organic part of geographical names when following the name (Atlantic Ocean, Dead Sea, Mississippi River).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize such terms when they are descriptive additions (the river Elbe, the desert of Sahara). Includes lists of terms capitalized in singular form only, singular/plural rules, and placement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 5: Adjectives/nouns distinguishing definite regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize adjectives and nouns used singly or together to distinguish definite regions when used with recognized geographical terms (Old World, Western Hemisphere, the East, the North).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize adjectives derived from such names when used as directions (oriental customs, the southern states); but capitalize when implying world-wide application (Eastern peoples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 6: Generic political-division terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of political divisions when they are organic parts of the proper name (Holy Roman Empire), when used integrally with 'of' (Department of the Lakes), or when used singly as accepted designations (the Union).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize such terms when standing alone or used paraphrastically (the empire, the state).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 7: Numbered political divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize numbered political divisions (Eleventh Congressional District, First Ward, Second Precinct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rule 100 for related conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 8: Names of thoroughfares, parks, buildings, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize the proper names of streets, parks, squares, blocks, buildings, and similar (Drexel Avenue, Lincoln Park, Capitol, White House).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize generic designations like courthouse, post-office, library except when part of the place name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 9: Names of parties, denominations, schools, and adherents
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of political parties, religious denominations, philosophical/literary/artistic schools and their adherents (Republican, Catholic, Epicurean, Symbolic school).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize when used in the general sense of a pervasive spirit or trend (republican form of government, evangelical spirit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 10: Monastic orders and members
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of monastic orders and their members (Black Friars, Dominican, Jesuit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 11: Proper (official) titles of organizations and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize official titles of organizations and institutions when used as the proper name (Union League Club, Smithsonian Institution, The Macmillan Company).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize generic terms when designating a class or when standing alone (the club, the association), except to avoid ambiguity or where clearly used in place of the true name (He joined the Hall [Tammany]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 12: Legislative, judiciary, administrative bodies and departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of governmental bodies and departments when specifically applied (Congress, Parliament, Supreme Court of the United States, Department of the Interior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize general or paraphrastic designations (the national assembly, the council, the department).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 13: Ordinals in certain designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize ordinals used to designate dynasties, sessions of Congress, regiments, etc. (Eighteenth Dynasty, Fifty-third Congress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes from cases like 'the Ming dynasty' where the dynasty name itself is used without ordinal capitalization rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 14: Historical epochs, language periods, geological ages
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize commonly accepted appellations for historical epochs and geological ages (Crusades, Renaissance, Pleistocene), with 'age' capitalized only when needed to avoid ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize informal adjectives in such phrases (early Algonkian). Abbreviations for Old English, Middle High German are noted (OE, MHG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 15: Names of important events
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of important events (Thirty Years' War, Revolution, War of 1812, Battle of Gettysburg, Louisiana Purchase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of wars, treaties, purchases as event names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 16: Political alliances and historically significant terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize political alliances and historical party/movement names that have acquired special significance (Protestant League, Holy Alliance, the Roses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to rule 9 for similar treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 17: Conventions, congresses, expositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of conventions, congresses, and expositions (Council of Nicaea, Parliament of Religions, Chicago World's Fair).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give examples with numbering and formal names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 18: Titles of treaties, acts, laws, juridical documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize specific titles of treaties, laws, acts, and juridical documents (Treaty of Verdun, Declaration of Independence, Magna Charta, Fourteenth Amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes difference in capitalization for 'the Constitution' of the United States when standing alone versus constitutions of other states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 19: Creeds and confessions of faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of creeds and confessions (Apostles' Creed, Nicene Creed, Augsburg Confession).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes exceptions such as 'ante-Nicene' (lowercase prefix) and cross-references to other rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 20: Civic holidays and ecclesiastical fast/feast days
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of civic holidays and feast/fast days (Fourth of July, Labor Day, Easter, Passover).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short forms (the Fourth) are acceptable in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 21: Titles of honor/respect and academic degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize official titles preceding a name and degrees following the name; capitalize titles of nobility and certain titles used alone when referring to a specific incumbent (President, King, Pope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize when the title follows the name (Woodrow Wilson, president of the United States) or when used with the article 'the' followed by a name that is not the existing incumbent; examples provide clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 22: Abbreviations like Ph.D., M.P., and celestial designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize and set without spaces abbreviations like Ph.D., M.P., F.R.G.S., and designations of celestial objects; these are set without spaces between letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references to rules 52, 103, 106 for spacing and related conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 23: One-letter abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize one-letter abbreviations except for units of measurement and minor literary subdivisions (R.V., C., A, but not p., I., n.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains convention and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 24: Names and pronouns referring to the Supreme Being
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize nouns and adjectives designating the Supreme Being or members of the Christian Trinity and pronouns referring to them when reference isn't closely preceded or followed by a distinctive name or clearly understood in context (the Almighty, Father, Son, Holy Ghost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize derived expressions (God's fatherhood -> father's is lowercase) in many common uses; guidance on pronoun capitalization depends on clarity and proximity to names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 25: Words with acquired, limited, or special meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize words with an acquired or special meaning used as specific institutional or degree designations (the Doctor's degree; a Freshman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize when general terms are used (the doctorate, a master in chancery) because explanatory modifiers remove the special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 26: Personified abstract ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize personified abstract ideas and similar terms (Nature wields her scepter; Vice in morality plays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to add emphasis when words are personified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 27: 'Father' for church father and 'Reformers' for Reformation leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'Fathers' and 'Reformers' when they denote church fathers or leaders of the Reformation where ambiguity would exist otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize generic descriptors like 'church reformers of the fifteenth century' when not used as a formal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 28: 'Church' in cited titles and specific edifices
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'Church' when part of properly cited titles of nationally organized bodies (Church of England) or part of a proper edifice name (Fifth Avenue Baptist Church).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize 'church' when standing alone in the general sense; note that exceptional capitalization may be used for rhetorical emphasis in arguments opposing Church and State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 29: Names for the Bible and other sacred books
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names for the Bible and other sacred books (Holy Scriptures, Koran, Vedas, Mishna).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize adjectives derived from these nouns (biblical, scriptural).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 30: Versions and editions of the Bible
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize specific versions and editions of the Bible (King James's Version, Authorized Version, Revised Version, Septuagint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides abbreviations (A.V., R.V., LXX) and conventions for usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 31: Books and divisions of sacred texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of books and divisions of the Bible and other sacred works when used as titles (Old Testament, Exodus, Psalms, Gospel of Luke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize generic terms like book, psalm, gospel when used generically (the five books of Moses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 32: Biblical parables
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of biblical parables (the parable of the Prodigal Son).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given as specific case under biblical capitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 33: Miscellaneous biblical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize terms with specific biblical significance (Last Supper, Eucharist, the Twelve, the Golden Rule, Kingdom of God).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate terms that are capitalized because of established usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 34: First word of sentence and first word of each line in English poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize the first word of a sentence and the first word of each line in English poetry; for Greek and Latin poetry, capitalize only the first word of a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show poetry capitalization conventions and the exception for classical verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 35: First word after a colon
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize the first word after a colon only when introducing a complete passage or sentence with independent meaning (summarizations, quotations, or when colon equates to 'as follows' or 'namely').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize when the quotation is closely connected with the preceding text, when the colon introduces a short explanatory phrase, or when it signals a note of comment; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 36: First word in enumerations
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, capitalize the first word of sections in an enumeration if any link contains two or more distinct clauses separated by semicolon, colon, or period, unless all are dependent on the same preceding term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of enumerations with capitalization depending on clause independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 37: Nouns followed by numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize nouns followed by numerals indicating order in a sequence (Room 16, Grade IV, Act I, Vol. I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize minor subdivisions of publications such as sec. 4, scene i, art. iii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 38: First word of a cited speech or thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize the first word of a cited speech or thought in direct discourse, whether preceded by a colon or comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show inline quotes and unquoted reported thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 39: First words after 'Whereas' and 'Resolved'
rubrics_metrics.description: In resolutions, capitalize the first words following 'Whereas' and 'Resolved' (Whereas, It has pleased God... Resolved, That ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting conventions noted for resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 40: Exclamations 'O' and 'Oh'
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize the exclamations 'O' and 'Oh' when used vocatively in direct address or exclamation ('O Lord!', 'Oh, that I were home again!').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to poetic capitalization rules (see 117).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 41: Principal words in English titles of publications and divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize all principal words (nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, verbs, first and last words) in English titles of publications and their divisions, subjects of lectures, and major heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes exceptions: some journals (Botanical Gazette) capitalize only first words and proper names for bibliographies; side-heads and certain headings have specific conventions (see 56, 172).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 42: Foreign titles capitalization conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: In foreign titles capitalize according to language conventions: Latin (proper nouns and derived adjectives), French/Italian/Spanish/Swedish/Norwegian (proper nouns only, not adjectives derived from them), German/Danish (capitalize all nouns), Dutch (capitalize all nouns and adjectives derived from proper nouns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for each language are provided (De amicitia; Histoire de la litterature frangaise; Geschichie des deutschen Feudalwesens; Geschiedenis der Nederlandsche Taal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 43: Definite article in newspaper/magazine titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not, as a rule, treat the definite article as part of the title when mentioning newspapers and magazines (the Chicago Tribune, the School Review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and conventional usage explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 44: Titles of ancient manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize titles of ancient manuscripts when cited (Codex Bemensis, Cod. Canonicianus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates abbreviation practices: MS (singular), MSS (plural).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 45: Nouns in hyphenated titles
rubrics_metrics.description: In titles with main words capitalized, capitalize all nouns forming parts of hyphenated compounds (Twentieth-Century Progress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not capitalize non-noun components; in side-heads only first word and proper nouns are capitalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 46: Scientific (Latin) names in botanical/zoological matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize scientific Latin names of divisions, orders, families, and genera (Cotylosauria, Felidae) but not their English derivatives (cotylosaurs, felids); species names capitalization depends on discipline (botanical/zoological vs geological/medical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples and notes (Felis ho, Rosa Carolina vs Pterygomatopus schmidti in geological contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 47: Names and epithets of peoples, races, tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names and epithets of peoples, races, and tribes (Kafir, Negro, Hottentot, Makassar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists typical ethnonyms and usage contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 48: Astronomical names
rubrics_metrics.description: In astronomical works, capitalize names of planets, stars, groups of stars, and catalog designations (Saturn, Ursa Major, M13, N.G.C. 6165), but not words like 'sun', 'earth', and 'moon' in general usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives catalog number examples and use of designations without spaces where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 49: University of Chicago internal names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize divisions, departments, officers, courses of study, and other official names of University of Chicago units in official work (the School of Education, the Board of Trustees, the President).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes usage of shortened forms (the School, the Department) and when to lower-case generic terms such as 'the division' in general references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 50: Use of capitals and small capitals in letters and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use capitals and small capitals for the names of town and state in the dateline, salutatory phrase, signature, and residence lines of letters; format specifics provided (Chicago, Ill., January 1, 1911; My dear Mr. Smith:).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains indention, centering, and type-size conventions; date line and address formatting guidance included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 51: Use of 'Whereas', 'Note', and 'Section' as set words
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize and set 'Whereas' in resolutions, 'Note' in notes (followed by period and dash), and 'Section' introducing paragraphs with numbering in constitutions/bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes usual abbreviation of 'Section' after first use and punctuation conventions (Section 1. ...; Sec 2. ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 52: Small capitals for A.M./P.M. and B.C./A.D.
rubrics_metrics.description: Set A.M., P.M., B.C., and A.D. in small capitals and without spaces between letters (11:30 A.M.; 53 B.C., 1906 A.D.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references to other rules on spacing and abbreviation conventions (22, 103, 106, 219).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rule 53: Use small (lower-case) initial letter for generalized derivatives of proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a small initial letter for words of common usage that were originally proper names and their derivatives where the origin is obscured and general usage has taken over (Utopia, bohemian, platonic) and for verbs derived from proper names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that verbs derived from proper names are not capitalized (see rule 1 i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of enumerated cross-references and index terms (index snippets)
rubrics_metrics.description: The index and contents list numerous cross-references and topics with page references (e.g., 'Small caps: defined, use of, in tabular work; Signatures: omission of comma after, rules for setting'), indicating granular style rules and indexing conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual's index entries reveal many micro-rules for spacing, hyphenation, divisions, type sizes, special character usage, and table formatting; these are to be consulted as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular and spacing micro-rules (index-derived)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous specific rules for spacing in tables, spacing around divisional signs, spacing of numerals, rules for leaders and braces, and standard spacing conventions for typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index references to rules 241–50, 258–73, 261–66, and specimens indicate precise formatting guidance for tabular work and spacing; consult those sections for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign-language titles and capitalization in lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed language-specific rules for capitalization in titles (Latin, French, Italian, Spanish, Scandinavian, German, Danish, Dutch) and for how to handle articles like 'the' in newspaper titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rule 42 and rule 43; examples provided for correct capitalization patterns in bibliographies and lists of publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of scientific names, italics, and species
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on capitalization and italicization of scientific names in botanical, zoological, paleontological, geological, and medical contexts (which ranks to capitalize, which to italicize, and discipline-specific exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references to rules 46 and 71 (italics) and examples provided throughout specimen and technical sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and compositorial practice (index and specimen guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific practical conventions for proofreaders and compositors including proofreader marks, duties of copyholders, and specimen type usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hints to Proofreaders, Hints to Copyholders, Proofreader's Marks (pages 125–133) and specimen sections for machine-specific instructions and character inventories.
